newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN seeks funds for 356,000 Palestinians in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: UN seeks funds for 356,000 Palestinians in Lebanon.

text.p: The United Nations launched an appeal on Thursday for $11 million to cover the urgent medical and educational needs of 356,000 Palestinians in Lebanon, most of whom lack jobs and access to the public health and school systems.

Peter Hansen, head of the U.N. Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), said the living standards of Palestinian refugees throughout the region had deteriorated since the peace process began three years ago.
Speaking after meeting officials from donor countries, the Dane said he had received promises for half of the $11 million.

The two-year appeal supplements UNRWA's regular $40 million budget for Lebanon, recovering from 17 years of civil war. The government provides no health, education or relief services to the Palestinians, leaving UNRWA as virtually the sole provider.
The funds will be used in part to pay hospitalisation for refugees. Some 1,000 patients face a waiting period of up to six months for surgery, according to the agency.
Health centres will be built in three of the 12 camps. New classrooms will be opened to lower the ratio of 53 pupils per teacher and a secondary school will be established at Tyre.
"Palestinian refugees all over the Middle East are suffering very, very severe deprivation," Hansen told a news conference.
At least 40 percent of Palestinian refugees in Lebanon are unemployed due to government restrictions in the job market, according to the agency, now based in Gaza City.

"Some 70 professions are reserved for Lebanese. That is another way of saying that Palestinians are not allowed," Hansen said. "That leaves very few jobs open to Palestinians -- construction and farm labour, basically."

Palestinian manual workers in agriculture and construction have lost a sizeable portion of their market share due to strong competition from migrant labourers coming into Lebanon from neighbouring Arab countries and the Far East, the UNRWA said.

"Since the Gulf War, Palestinians in Lebanon have lost employment opportunities in the Gulf and if they travel abroad they run the risk of not being readmitted to Lebanon," Hansen said. "We are in a phase of the peace process where refugees in Lebanon and elsewhere have little to look at in terms of gains."
